Article Title: 'West Bengal' may soon become 'Paschim Banga'; state BJP chief says Bill coming
Article Text:
West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya says the state will soon be renamed Paschim Banga

NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya on Wednesday said that the state is set to be renamed “Paschim Banga”, addint that a legislative bill would be introduced in the first session of assemby."How many times must I say, brother? The name will be 'Paschim Banga'," news agency ANI quoted him saying after he was asked about the name change again.He had also indicated earlier this week that the formal renaming was imminent, saying names such as “Paschim Bangla”, “Bangla” and “Banga” would no longer be used.“Yes, absolutely. Paschim Banga Bhavan... West Bengal's 'Paschim'... For a long time now, you will no longer have to hear names like 'Paschim Bangla', 'Bangla', or 'Banga'. 'Paschim Banga' (West Bengal) is coming,” Bhattacharya had said on Monday.Explaining the proposed legislative move, the BJP state chief said the bill would seek to link the state's official name with its historical identity.“Very soon, in the very first session itself, our government is introducing a bill so that the name of this state remains intrinsically linked with the history of this state, and that remains its identity.That is why the state is going to be named 'Paschim Banga',” he said.The proposal to rename West Bengal has a long political history. The move dates back to 1999, when the Left Front government proposed ‘Paschim Banga’ as the state's new name.The proposal was later changed to ‘Bangla’ after then Congress MLA Saugata Roy suggested it, but the Centre rejected it.After the Trinamool Congress came to power in 2011, the state again proposed ‘Paschim Banga’, which was turned down by the UPA-2 government.In 2016, the state suggested three names, ‘Bangla’ in Bengali, ‘Bengal’ in English and ‘Bangal’ in Hindi, before eventually proposing ‘Bangla’ in all three languages.In July 2018, the West Bengal assembly passed a resolution to rename the state ‘Bangla’ and sent it to the Centre for approval. However, the proposal was not cleared.The Centre cited the need for a constitutional amendment, while sources had earlier said the similarity between ‘Bangla’ and Bangladesh could cause confusion at international forums.In 2019, then Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai told the Rajya Sabha that the Centre had not approved the name change.
Article Summary: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya says the state is set to be renamed ‘Paschim Banga’ He adds that a legislative bill would be introduced in the first session of assemby. He had indicated earlier this week that the formal renaming was imminent.

Article Title: Ashok Chakra for flydubai pilot Smit Machchar? Rajya Sabha MP Kartikeya Sharma urges PM Modi
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha member seeks Ashok Chakra for Indian pilot Smit Machchar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member Kartikeya Sharma has written to PM Modi , urging him to consider awarding the country's highest peacetime gallantry award, the 'Ashok Chakra' to flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchar for his courage and presence of mind midair during a hijacking attempt made by Omani co-pilot.Machchar was critically injured during flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30 after his co-pilot attacked him and attempted to take control of the aircraft.Despite suffering severe injuries, Machchar remained focused on protecting the 174 passengers on board and continued to carry out his duties under extreme circumstances.Sharma said Machchar's courage and composure during the crisis reflected the "indomitable spirit" and dedication to duty of Indians. He said the captain put the safety of passengers ahead of his own well-being despite being seriously injured.The Rajya Sabha member said recognising Machchar at the national level would not only honour his bravery but also inspire young people across the country. He added that every Indian was proud of the captain's courage.Sharma urged Prime Minister Modi to consider conferring the 'Ashok Chakra' on Machchar in recognition of his bravery and dedication to duty.The letter comes days after the alleged hijacking attempt aboard flydubai flight FZ1073. According to reports, Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Machchar with an axe inside the cockpit in an attempt to bring down the aircraft.Despite suffering serious injuries, Machchar managed to unlatch the cockpit door, allowing passengers and off-duty crew members to enter and restrain the co-pilot.The confrontation caused the aircraft to enter a steep descent, with the plane dropping around 16,000 feet in two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was sent.The aircraft was later diverted and made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 180 people on board disembarked safely.A Times of Israel report published on Sunday said al-Hammami had planned to direct the aircraft towards Israel's Ben Gurion Airport.The report, citing Hebrew media sources, said the Omani co-pilot was detained and was being interrogated in the United Arab Emirates.
Article Summary: Rajya Sabha member seeks Ashok Chakra for Indian pilot Smit Machchar. Machchar was critically injured during flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30. Omani co- pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Machchar with an axe.

Article Title: 'Unable to distinguish between victim & perpetrator': India tears into OIC over J&K remarks at UN
Article Text:
Biplab Deb counters OIC over J&K, terror remarks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India hit back at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) at the UN General Assembly, rejecting its remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and New Delhi’s actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.West Tripura Lok Sabha MP Biplab Kumar Deb, delivering India’s national statement at the UNGA Sixth Committee on Tuesday said the OIC had failed to distinguish between those responsible for terrorism and its victims.“I also address now the statement delivered by the chair of the OIC on India's focused and measured actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, from where terrorist attacks against India were planned and directed,” news agency PTI quoted Deb saying.He added that it is “regrettable that those delivering the statement” are “unable to separate fact from fiction and distinguish between victim and perpetrator”.India asserted that it has the right to defend its citizens against cross-border terrorism and warned that there would be consequences for those who engage in terrorism.Deb also objected to what he called the OIC’s “unwarranted reference” to Jammu and Kashmir.He urged the grouping to instead focus on Pakistan’s “illegal occupation” and alleged rights violations in PoK.“The OIC chair would do better to focus on Pakistan's illegal occupation, especially in Rawalakot, where wanton killings, brutal violence and the denial of basic rights to the people living there are so visible. Such willful blindness only speaks of bigotry and intolerance,” he said.Saudi Arabia had delivered the OIC statement at the Sixth Committee, which deals with legal issues. The OIC referred to “military escalation in Southeast Asia” and “unjustified strikes” at multiple locations in Pakistan, without naming India.India’s response came as it reiterated its position that cross-border terrorism remains a persistent threat. Deb cited the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 civilians were killed, and said the attack demonstrated the human cost of terrorism.“The Pahalgam terror attack was a calculated assault on our sovereignty, planned and executed by networks that continue to enjoy state patronage, safe havens, and material and logistical support from across our western border,” he said.Deb also called terrorism one of the gravest threats to international peace and security, stressing that there could be no justification for attacks on civilians.“Terrorism is antithetical to the values of the UN. There can be no justification whatsoever for deliberately targeting civilians. There is no distinction between good and bad terrorism,” he said.
Article Summary: India hits back at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) at the UN General Assembly. West Tripura Lok Sabha MP Biplab Kumar Deb said the OIC had failed to distinguish between those responsible for terrorism and its victims. He urged the grouping to instead focus on Pakistan’s “illegal occupation” and alleged rights violations in PoK.

Article Title: KPSC recruitment case: Suspended chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, member BV Geetha detained
Article Text:
KPSC Case: ED Arrests Suspended Chairman Sahukar, Member Geetha

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Tuesday detained suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukar and KPSC member BV Geetha after conducting searches at Sahukar's residence in Dollars Colony, Sanjaynagar.Last week, the ED completed questioning suspended IAS officer and former KPSC controller of examinations Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar after taking him into custody. Another accused in the case, self-styled political activist Basavaraj Kannale, was also questioned by the agency. Both Gangwar and Kannale are currently in judicial custody at Bengaluru Central Prison after their bail pleas were rejected by the courts.On Tuesday morning, a team of ED officials reached Sahukar's residence and recorded his statement. He was detained later in the evening. Another ED team picked up KPSC member BV Geetha from her flat in an apartment in Dollars Colony, Sanjaynagar, for questioning.The ED had earlier recorded statements from several candidates, including Suguresh, a close relative of Sahukar who had secured unusually high marks, according to the FIR.Sources said Sahukar was detained based on Suguresh's confession.The investigation has also found that Sahukar allegedly called Gangwar twice on the night of January 7, a day before the examination. Gangwar is accused of sharing the question paper and an answer script with Suguresh, who allegedly later shared them with Geetha.Sahukar, a native of Hemanala village in Raichur district's Devadurga taluk, holds a degree in Agricultural Engineering. He was appointed as a KPSC member in September 2019 and was elevated as chairman in April 2021 by then governor Vajubhai Vala on the recommendation of the state government, succeeding Shadakshari Swamy.Sahukar has also faced scrutiny in a separate case involving allegations that his daughter submitted a fraudulent income certificate showing an annual family income of Rs 40,000 to claim reservation under Category 3B for government employment.The Karnataka High Court had criticised the declaration as a "fraud" and an "eyewash", observing that Sahukar was drawing a substantial salary as KPSC chairman. He was subsequently suspended from office following cabinet recommendations.He is also under investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) over alleged irregularities, paper leaks and cash-for-jobs cases linked to recruitment examinations, including the recruitment of 400 veterinary officers and other gazetted posts.The investigations have alleged the involvement of middlemen and illegal transactions in exchange for candidate selections. His anticipatory bail plea was earlier rejected by the High Court after the CID presented evidence allegedly linking him and his associates to middlemen.The ED is investigating the money-laundering aspects of the alleged recruitment scams and has conducted searches as part of its probe into the financial trail and suspected illicit assets.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) detained suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukar and KPSC member BV Geetha. The ED is investigating the money-laundering aspects of the alleged recruitment scams and has conducted searches as part of its probe.

Article Title: 'Congress loses even on ballot papers': Himanta hails NDA's Silchar civic polls victory
Article Text:
BJP-led NDA sweeps first Silchar civic polls with 34 seats

NEW DELHI: The ruling BJP-led NDA won the first elections to the Silchar Municipal Corporation on Tuesday, securing 34 of the 42 seats.Reacting to the result, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said Congress performs poorly even when elections are held through paper ballots.“See, Congress loses even on paper ballots. In fact, Congress loses even more on paper ballots. That’s why in EVMs, sometimes people go and press NOTA or get panicked seeing the machine and vote in the wrong place. But people are well-practiced in voting on paper ballots. So whenever voting happens on paper ballots, Congress loses even more,” Sarma said.Polling for the 40 wards was held on October 3, while BJP candidates Bijendra Prasad Singh and Bhakti Sen Talukdar were elected unopposed from wards 9 and 20, respectively. Counting of votes began at 8 am, with ballot papers used in the elections.Sarma said the verdict reflected the people's faith in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and his vision for urban governance under the Viksit Bharat initiative."Another day, another win for @BJP4Assam! The people of Silchar have given us a thumping majority in the Silchar Municipal Corporation elections, held through BALLOT PAPER," Sarma said in a post on X.He thanked the people of Silchar for the “resounding mandate” and reiterated his government's commitment to making the city “one of Assam's foremost cities”.Assam BJP president Dilip Saikia said the results showed that Congress had failed to win public support even in an election conducted through ballot papers."The Congress always complains about EVM tampering, but this election was held through ballot papers, and they are nowhere," he told reporters.The BJP won 32 seats, while its ally Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) secured two. The Congress won two seats and Independents six, officials said. The BJP has sought recounting in two wards, 29 and 30, where an Independent candidate and a Congress candidate, respectively, emerged victorious. A decision on the demand is yet to be taken, they said.A total of 133 candidates contested the elections. The BJP fielded candidates in 38 wards, the AGP in four and the Congress in 38, while 52 Independents and one CPI(M) candidate were also in the fray.The Silchar Municipal Board was upgraded to a 42-ward municipal corporation in 2022 and became operational in June 2025. Silchar, the principal city of the Barak Valley, had remained without an elected civic body for six years.Poor road conditions, inadequate drainage, waterlogging, erratic power supply and irregular drinking water supply were among the key issues raised during the campaign.
Article Summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said Congress performs poorly even when elections are held through paper ballots. The BJP won 32 seats, while its ally Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) secured two. The Congress won two seats and Independents six, officials said.

Article Title: Punjab government moves Supreme Court against CBI probe into 'bribe syndicate' linked to CM Bhagwant Mann's OSD
Article Text:
Supreme Court said the state’s petition will be listed for hearing either Wednesday or Thursday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Hours before CBI carried out searches at Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann 's camp office in Chandigarh and registered an FIR against his OSD and others, Punjab govt had rushed Supreme Court to urgently hear its appeal against Punjab and Haryana HC's Monday order directing the agency to probe ED's allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through an OSD in the CM's office.Fearing imminent coercive action - based on the HC order for registration of an FIR - by CBI against top politicians and bureaucrats in the state, the Mann-led AAP govt in its appeal sought an urgent stay of the HC's directions. "If the impugned judgement is not stayed, CBI will register an FIR against high public functionaries of the state on untested material... and the situation will become irreversible," it said.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the state govt, said HC had brushed aside the state's preliminary objections, declined three weeks to Punjab Police to complete the preliminary inquiry, which it initiated based on ED's communication levelling "cash-for-transfers postings" allegation, and directed a CBI probe, contrary to the federal scheme of governance mandated by the Constitution."Please hear the petition today itself at 2pm," Singh requested a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.When the bench said it was impossible to take the appeal for hearing Tuesday itself, Singh said the appeal must be heard Wednesday, suggesting the development can have potentially a huge political fallout in the poll-bound state and arguing that the order marked a breach of the federal scheme of governance.The bench said the state's petition will be listed for hearing either Wednesday or Thursday.In its appeal, the state govt revealed ED's Jalandhar zonal office on July 30 sent a 150-page communication to Punjab DGP under PMLA, alleging it was found that one Nihal Gohal, whose premises were searched in May, influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions "through an officer on special duty in the office of CM".DGP marked the communication, large parts of which were illegible, to Punjab Bureau of Investigation on Aug 3. The bureau began its preliminary inquiry within two days and started collecting evidence from different departments. It sent reminders to ED on Aug 28, Sept 2 and Sept 5, asking it to depute an officer with complete records, but no cooperation was received till Sept 7, the state claimed.HC had ordered a CBI probe because of what it held to be inaction in the registeration of an FIR on the material evidence sent by ED and had said, "Prima facie allegations with regard to scams including cash for transfers, cash for getting favourable policies, cash for tenders, and such other illegal activities corruption in high public offices have been substantiated by ED with reference to various WhatsApp chats and other information. .."Punjab govt said the high court erred by sending CBI into a state which had withdrawn consent to the agency needed to carry out an investigation in the state's jurisdiction, without citing any exceptional circumstances that warranted a CBI probe.In 2010, SC had ruled that SC and HCs can direct a CBI probe in exceptional cases even in states which have withdrawn general consent.
Article Summary: Punjab govt rushed Supreme Court to urgently hear its appeal against Punjab and Haryana HC's Monday order directing the agency to probe ED's allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through an OSD in the CM's office. HC had ordered a CBI probe because of what it held to be inaction in the registeration of an FIR.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: Arms & drugs seized in cross-border smuggling case; 4 held
Article Text:

JAMMU: J&K Police have arrested four suspects, including one from Punjab, in connection with the alleged cross-border smuggling of drugs and arms via drones in the border village of Arnia in Jammu district. An Italy-made Beretta pistol, two magazines, four live rounds, and over 1kg of narcotics were seized during subsequent searches, police said Tuesday.On Oct 3, cops manning a checkpoint at Arnia’s Tamala Bridge stopped two men moving on a bike around 10.45pm. One of the men, Rahul Kumar, was found carrying 264g of suspected heroin, a Beretta pistol, two magazines and four live rounds. Another 276g of suspected heroin was seized from the second man, Ajay Kumar Talhar. Both are residents of Arnia.During questioning, the accused allegedly confessed their links with Pakistan-based handlers and admitted to having received two air-dropped consignments in the past. Information obtained from the duo led cops to a third suspect, also named Ajay Kumar. He was arrested with 464g of opium resin and 13.3g of heroin, police said.Further probe revealed the involvement of a fourth suspect—Jaganpreet Randhawa alias Jaggi, believed to be a forward link in the smuggling nexus—who was arrested in Punjab.Arnia PS registered an FIR under relevant sections of the NDPS and Arms Acts. Officials said further investigation was underway.Many such cases have earlier been reported from forward areas along the Indo-Pak international border and the Line of Control in J&K. The probes were later handed over to NIA due to the magnitude of the smuggled contraband, arms and ammunition.
Article Summary: J&K Police have arrested four suspects, including one from Punjab, in connection with the alleged cross-border smuggling of drugs and arms via drones. An Italy- made Beretta pistol, two magazines, four live rounds, and over 1kg of narcotics were seized during subsequent searches.

Article Title: CM Samrat Choudhary reviews Bihar flood situation, seeks damage report
Article Text:
Bihar has been hit hard by severe floods caused by unprecedented water levels in rivers, leading Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to assess the situation closely.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary ordered authorities to provide a thorough report as soon as possible, after reviewing the state's flood situation and the devastation it caused.A news release states that BJP national president and MP Nitin Nabin attended the review meeting, which took place in the "Sankalp" auditorium at Lok Sevak Awas.During the meeting, water resources department secretary Dr Chandrashekhar Singh briefed Choudhary on the causes of the floods and the situation that developed in the state in two phases.In the first phase, the Ganga, Son, Ghaghra, Kosi and Punpun rivers recorded their highest-ever water levels compared with previous records.During the second phase, excessive rainfall led to the Gandak River reaching record water levels at four locations. Embankment damage was reported at six locations across West Champaran, Gopalganj and Saran districts.Santosh Kumar Mall, Principal Secretary of the Disaster Management Department, gave a briefing to the group about the relief and rescue efforts conducted during the floods.According to Choudhary, this year's extraordinarily high water levels in the Ganga, Gandak, and Son rivers compared to prior years created a major flood situation.He also identified silt accumulation in riverbeds as one of the major factors contributing to the floods. The Chief Minister noted that Bihar was the first state in the country to formulate a silt policy.In order to expedite relief, rehabilitation, and necessary development work in affected areas, the chief minister instructed officials to keep a close eye on the current state of rivers and the damage caused by the floods. He also ordered that a preliminary detailed report on the damage caused by the floods be submitted as soon as possible, according to ANI report.On October 12, 2026, Choudhary announced that households impacted by the second phase of the floods will get ex-gratia assistance.Additionally, he instructed the Disaster Management Department to work with all relevant agencies to evaluate the damage caused by the floods and the estimated cost of repair, and to submit the report as soon as possible.In light of potential issues, officials were also instructed to make the required preparations following the draining of water from flood-affected regions.Senior officials included Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, Agriculture Department Principal Secretary Narmadeshwar Lal, Disaster Management Minister Ratnesh Sada, Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, and Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary were present in the meeting.Meanwhile, on Saturday, October 3, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary gave the Disaster Management Department instructions to guaranty the prompt delivery of relief supplies to flood-affected and inaccessible areas of Saran district, with special air-dropping operations being conducted in cooperation with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Defense.The Chief Minister's Office reports that 15 Indian Air Force helicopter missions have delivered over 28 tons of food supplies, including more than 5,600 dry ration packages, into flood-affected districts of Saran district. In accordance with Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's directives, the Disaster Management Department organized the air-dropping operations in collaboration with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Defense to guaranty the prompt delivery of vital food supplies to flood-affected and inaccessible areas.The initiative was aimed at reaching affected areas where road connectivity had been disrupted. The Disaster Management Department and district administration are continuously monitoring the flood situation, while alternative modes of transportation are being used alongside road routes wherever required.The administration is working to ensure that essential relief materials and food supplies reach every flood-affected family as quickly as possible.Pilots and personnel from various Indian Air Force units have been involved in the relief operation. The air-dropping mission is being conducted under the leadership of Group Captain Anuj Gupta and Wing Commander Vishal Khatri (Gorakhpur), Squadron Leader Rohit Dadarwal, Flight Lieutenant Kunal Kalamkar (Bagdogra) and Flight Lieutenant Rathore Bharat Singh (Bagdogra).Choudhary expressed gratitude to the Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Defence and the Indian Air Force for delivering relief supplies to flood-affected people in Bihar during the crisis.He said relief and rescue operations were being carried out effectively in the affected areas through coordinated efforts by the Central and state governments.
Article Summary: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary ordered authorities to provide a thorough report as soon as possible. Article Title: US House introduces resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, condemns 'act of terrorism'
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar is recovering in Abu Dhabi hospital from multiple injuries

Resolved, That the House of Representatives— (1) honors Captain Smit Machchhar for extraordinary courage in protecting every soul aboard his aircraft; (2) commends the heroic actions of the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down; (3) wishes Captain Machchhar and all who were injured a full recovery; (4) condemns the attack on Flydubai Flight 1073 as an act of terrorism and as an attack on the safety of international civil aviation; and (5) calls for a full and expeditious investigation by the Governments of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed.

The US House of Representatives have introduced a resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar who was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami on September 30.The resolution introduced as "Honoring Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, and condemning the attempted terrorist attack on that flight" by Josh Gottheimer, Don Bacon and Michael McCaul, described the incident and hailed Machchhar."On September 30, 2026, Flydubai Flight 1073 departed Dubai International Airport for Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, Israel, carrying approximately 174 passengers, the majority of them Israeli citizens, including 4 United States citizens and 27 children," it stated."Whereas, midway through the flight, the first officer attacked the captain on the flight deck with the aircraft’s emergency crash axe and attempted to seize the flight controls, and the aircraft lost more than 14,000 feet of altitude in under 30 seconds," it desribed the incident. Whereas Captain Smit Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and, despite grave injuries, used his remaining strength to unlock the cockpit door so that off-duty pilots could enter and land the aircraft and so that crew and passengers could restrain the first officer; Whereas the aircraft landed safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia with all passengers and crew accounted for; and Whereas, on October 3, 2026, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the Emirati investigation had determined that the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act," it added.Then it went to resolve as follows:On September 30, Flydubai Flight FZ1073, carrying more than 170 passengers and crew from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was forced into an emergency diversion after the co-pilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar in the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft.The plane rapidly lost altitude before Machchhar, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker; two off-duty pilots then helped land the aircraft safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The UAE subsequently launched an investigation, and on October 3 its Attorney General said the probe had found that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act. Investigators are continuing to examine the circumstances, motive, possible links and physical and digital evidence, with authorities in other countries also looking into the incident.
Article Summary: The US House of Representatives have introduced a resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar who was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot Hamam al- Hammami on September 30. The resolution introduced by Josh Gottheimer, Don Bacon and Michael McCaul, described the incident and hailedMachchhar.

Article Title: Teen couple commit suicide on Instagram live in Gujarat forest; family among viewers
Article Text:
A man and a 16-year-old girl ended their lives in Dahod district





VADODARA: A man and a 16-year-old girl, who were in a relationship, hanged themselves on Sunday — while livestreaming on Instagram — in a forested area of Singvad taluka in Dahod district. Their families and the 50-odd people watching the stream were left horrified.Police officials said Rajesh Ninama (22) was having an affair with the girl. “Rajesh had taken the girl to meet his parents a few days ago and sought their permission for marriage. His parents allegedly refused, as both were from the same clan, with the same surname,” said Shailesh Baria, a police officer from Randhikpur police station.The couple, residents of Limkheda taluka, were upset and resolved to end their lives. On Sunday morning, they went to a forested area in Haripur village of Singvad taluka around 10 am. Rajesh turned on his Instagram live and looped a long piece of cloth over a branch. They then hanged themselves.Police were informed, went to the spot and brought down the bodies. “They didn’t leave any suicide note behind. We are investigating if there was any other reason behind their extreme step,” Baria said.

Article Title: Grandfather shoots lawyer grandson in Lonavla over property: How blood splatters exposed grisly killing inside hotel
Article Text:
Pune Rural police arrested Motiram Marathe on the charge of shooting dead his grandson Abhay Marathe (33) on Monday.

What happened at the hotel

Blood stains raised further questions

Dispute over property sale

CCTV cameras allegedly removed

Two licensed rifles





PUNE: A family’s account of a Lonavla lawyer’s death as an accidental shooting began to unravel after police examining his body found that the bullet wound did not appear consistent with the version they had been given.The discovery led investigators to the hotel where 33-year-old lawyer Abhay Marathe was allegedly shot dead during a dispute over the sale of a property, police said.His 83-year-old grandfather, Motiram Marathe, was arrested on Monday on the charge of murder. Four other relatives were arrested for allegedly destroying evidence, Pune Rural police said.Lonavla City police were alerted by a hospital on Monday afternoon that Abhay, from Bhushi, had died from a bullet injury.His family told doctors and police that he had been cleaning Motiram’s 12-bore rifle inside their hotel when it accidentally went off. The bullet hit Abhay in the chest, killing him instantly.Police initially registered an accidental death case.But when Abhay’s body was sent to Sassoon General Hospital in Pune for post-mortem, Superintendent of Police (Pune Rural) Sandeep Singh Gill, additional superintendent Shubham Kumar and local crime branch inspector Pramod Kshirsagar examined the injury.“Self-inflicted or accidental firearm injuries are different from the injury we found on Abhay. In an accidental firing, it is unlikely for a rifle bullet to hit the chest,” Gill said.The crime branch then went to the hotel where the shooting was said to have taken place.Investigators found a pool of blood on the wall beside the hotel counter and another pool nearby. Blood splatters were also visible on a wall about five feet above the ground.“This increased our suspicion that Abhay was shot dead inside the hotel,” Gill said.Police questioned the hotel workers and manager, who told them about a dispute between Abhay and his grandfather over the sale of a property.Motiram had opposed the sale of the property, police said.“They again had a heated argument over the issue around 11.30am on Monday. Abhay allegedly charged at his grandfather during the argument. Motiram then took out his licensed rifle and shot his grandson dead,” Gill said.Police allege that the family then tried to make the shooting appear accidental.Gill said Abhay’s sister, uncle, aunt and cousin were alerted after the shooting and came to the hotel.They allegedly moved Abhay’s body into one of the rooms before removing the CCTV cameras and digital video recorder (DVR) and hiding them.“They threatened the hotel employees against revealing anything. Thereafter, they informed Abhay’s parents about the incident,” Gill said. The four relatives — Rajashri Pawar, 58; Hiraman Marathe, 54; Kavita Marathe, Hiraman’s wife; and Manoj Marathe, 32 — were arrested for allegedly destroying evidence.Police said Motiram had two licensed rifles. He obtained the licences in 1970 for hunting.The accused have been charged under sections 103 (murder), 238 (causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender) and 241 (destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with sections of the Indian Arms Act.
Article Summary: Lawyer Abhay Marathe, 33, was allegedly shot dead during a dispute over the sale of a property. His 83-year-old grandfather Motiram Marathe was arrested on Monday on the charge of murder. Four other relatives were arrested for allegedly destroying evidence.

Article Title: Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen faced an unexpected $1,000,000 lawsuit weeks after their wedding over a shocking Costa Rica incident
Article Text:
Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen faced an unexpected $1,000,000 lawsuit (Getty Images)

Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen faced $1 million claims after the Costa Rica incident

Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen later faced FTX investor lawsuit

Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen had only been married for weeks when their Costa Rica wedding celebrations turned into a legal fight. In Sept. 2009, two photographers and Agence France-Presse sued the former couple for at least $1 million. They accused security guards linked to the couple of confronting them and firing at their car after they took pictures near the property.The case drew attention because it involved Tom Brady, Gisele Bündchen, their wedding celebrations and an alleged shooting. But the lawsuit never went to trial in New York. On May 26, 2010, Judge Judith Gische dismissed the case, saying New York did not have jurisdiction over the couple.The dispute began during an April 2009 celebration at Gisele Bündchen’s holiday home in Costa Rica. Photographer Yuri Cortez, who worked for Agence France-Presse, and Rolando Aviles of Costa Rican newspaper Al Dia went to cover the couple.The photographers claimed that security guards approached them and demanded their cameras and memory cards. According to their lawsuit, they refused and headed back to their vehicle.They then alleged that security guards fired at the car, damaging its rear windshield.Cortez, Aviles and Agence France-Presse sought at least $1 million in damages when they filed the lawsuit in September 2009. Their complaint also accused Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen of responsibility for the actions of the security team.Brady strongly denied the shooting allegation.In a 2009 interview with Sports Illustrated, while discussing the Costa Rica incident, Brady called the photographers' claims “absolute total b.s.” He also said, “Our security guys didn't even have guns. There were no shots fired.”That gave the case two sharply different accounts. The photographers described a frightening confrontation, while Brady denied that anyone fired a weapon.The legal fight then moved to the question of where the case belonged. The photographers filed in New York, but Judge Judith Gische dismissed the case on May 26, 2010. She said Brady and Bündchen lived in Massachusetts and that the alleged incident happened in Costa Rica.Gische also dismissed the claims against Gisele Bündchen, finding no evidence that she had been involved in hiring or directing the security guards. The ruling did not determine whether the photographers' allegations were true. It only meant the New York court would not hear the case.The Costa Rican legal proceedings involving the security guards continued separately.More than a decade later, Brady and Bündchen found themselves connected to another high-profile lawsuit, this time over cryptocurrency exchange FTX.After FTX collapsed in Nov. 2022, investors sued several celebrities who promoted the company, including Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen. The plaintiffs argued that celebrity endorsements helped attract customers and alleged violations tied to FTX's business and securities offerings.The case later narrowed. In May 2025, a federal judge dismissed many claims against the celebrity defendants but allowed some claims under Florida and Oklahoma law to continue, according to Reuters.The FTX case differs sharply from the 2009 wedding lawsuit. The earlier case centered on allegations involving security guards at the couple's Costa Rica property, while the later litigation focused on Brady and Bündchen's promotional relationship with FTX.
Article Summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen faced $1 million lawsuit after Costa Rica wedding. Photographer and Agence France-Presse accused security guards of firing at their car. Case never went to trial in New York because New York did not have jurisdiction over the couple. Brady later faced FTX investor lawsuit.

DEHRADUN: An 80-year-old retired works manager at an ordnance factory in Dehradun was allegedly murdered along with his wife and their house help at their home on Tuesday.Police arrested Raj Kumar , a plumber from Uttar Pradesh’s Bijnor who had been working in Dehradun for around five years, in connection with the killings.The victims were identified as Ramesh Kapoor, his wife Rajni, 75, and their house help Tilya Devi, 48. Article Title: Gujarat: Lover forced into sex act with woman in public as ‘punishment’ for affair
Article Text:
Representative image





RAJKOT: In a horrifying case of vigilante brutality, a man was allegedly forced to perform sexual acts with a married woman with whom he was in a relationship and made to drink her urine as “punishment” in public glare as a so-called “purification ritual” in Surendranagar.The woman and her partner were allegedly subjected to the ordeal by her husband and his relatives on Oct 4. The accused also recorded the acts on mobile phones and circulated the videos on social media.Police traced the woman after coming across the viral videos and arrested nine people, including her husband and his relatives.According to the complaint, the woman was married to a man in Vapi. She had left her husband and moved to Chotila, where she lived with her partner for around three months. Her family later traced her, brought her back to Vapi and allegedly confined her in a house. She eventually escaped and returned to Chotila five days ago.When her husband learnt that she was back with her partner, he allegedly alerted his relatives, who traced the couple, brought them to a house in Surendranagar and subjected them to the alleged “purification ritual”.Talking to TOI, Surendranagar DSP Premsukh Delu said police learnt about the incident after a community leader alerted them and videos of the assault surfaced on social media.“I received a call from a community leader regarding a woman who had been brutalised. We also came across several videos. Several police teams were deployed to trace the woman,” Delu said.Police teams searched houses in the area and found the woman at one of them. “She started crying on seeing the police. We matched her face with the woman in the video and brought her to the police station. She narrated her ordeal after counselling,” Delu said.According to the complaint, the accused brought the couple to Surendranagar, claiming they were going to perform a “purification ritual”. They allegedly beat them with wooden sticks and thrashed them. The man was then tied to a tree with a rope, while the woman was confined to a room.The accused allegedly later forced the man to perform sexual acts with the woman in a verandah and subjected both to further humiliation. The man was also allegedly forced to drink the woman’s urine. The entire ordeal was recorded on a mobile phone and the videos circulated on social media, police said.RM Sangada, inspector, A-Division police station, said police are also investigating who recorded the videos and circulated them on social media.The accused have been booked under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including Sections 70(1) (sexual intercourse by deceitful means), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 127(3) (wrongful confinement), 142 (wrongfully concealing or keeping a kidnapped/abducted person) and 3(5) (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention), as well as provisions of the IT Act.
